title: Immediate retry silently discards a staged-only record edit
detail: Material (F1): with the last committed dispatch unchanged in the working tree but different bytes staged for that same path, select_record reuses it without inspecting the index. Real Spacedock 0.27.2 then runs path-scoped git add -A, replacing the staged blob; exit 0, MM becomes clean, HEAD stays unchanged. Reproduced independently twice at 0d84d5d1b96fd674dba3a442d69c2e7898cceccd.
fix: Before identical committed-record reuse, refuse when the index entry differs from HEAD; preserve bytes and index, and add a regression for this retry path.
released_user_and_normal_workflow: FO uses the accepted immediate retry after a successful stamped dispatch while the shared state checkout contains a partially staged edit to that same record.
observable_harm: The staged dispatch annotation is removed from the index without a new commit or warning; staged information is lost from the ordinary Git workflow.
affected_boundary: contract[kc-dev-flow-2/references/profiles/pilot.md#pilot-bounded-real-use]: cover data safety in the accepted persistence/retry journey; implementation-1-message-3 requires refusing nonidentical existing records without altering staging.
trigger_evidence: retry-index-probe.json and captain-run/retry-index.json: exit 0; index_preserved false; status MM -> empty. retry-index-control.json: a throwaway index check refuses with exit 1 and leaves all state unchanged.
